resources.string: One window remains dark. Its maker’s name has vanished from the brass frame. A paper moth waits beside three traces: a broken seal, a thread of light, and a clockwork keeper.
Under the broken seal, an inscription survives. You restore the missing name and the window answers with light.
The seal cannot be read, but its reverse bears a workshop mark. You follow it to a spare lantern and carry its light back to the window.
The thread crosses an invisible bridge. At its end, a lantern preserves the name you came to find. You bring it home.
The thread fades before the bridge appears. Below it, a narrow passage leads to the lamp room. You recover a light by another route.
The keeper remembers a name and a promise. You listen to both before returning the lantern to its place.
The keeper cannot recall the name. It asks you to shelter a nameless lantern instead. You accept, and the window glows all the same.
A light recovered through a choice of your own. An original tale from the Hall, not a memory extracted from your books.
